functions.name: InitializeMemoryAllocator
functions.comment:
Initializes a memory allocator with virtual memory management and free list structures.

Algorithm:
1. Check global allocator mode (g_nAllocatorMode) to determine allocation strategy
2. If mode is -1, use static global error table offset (g_aErrorTable + 0x12)
3. Otherwise, allocate 0x2020 bytes from heap for descriptor structure
4. Reserve 4MB (0x400000) of virtual address space with MEM_RESERVE flag
5. Commit first 64KB (0x10000) with PAGE_READWRITE protection
6. Initialize allocator descriptor linking to global error table chain
7. Setup memory structure pointers: base, end, free list start
8. Initialize 1024 (0x400) free list entries with size masks and patterns
9. Clear committed memory region to zero
10. Setup memory blocks with headers and free list linkage
11. Return pointer to allocator descriptor on success, NULL on failure

Parameters:
None

Returns:
ErrorTableEntry * - Pointer to allocator descriptor on success, NULL on failure
  - Success: Valid pointer to initialized memory allocator structure
  - Error: NULL if heap allocation fails or virtual memory allocation fails

Special Cases:
- Static mode (g_nAllocatorMode == -1): Uses pre-allocated global structure
- Dynamic mode (g_nAllocatorMode != -1): Allocates new descriptor from heap
- Memory allocation failures trigger cleanup of partial allocations
- Error table is repurposed as allocator descriptor structure

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x2020 (8224 decimal) - Heap allocation size for allocator descriptor
0x400000 (4194304 decimal) - Virtual memory reservation size (4MB)
0x10000 (65536 decimal) - Initial committed memory size (64KB)  
0x2000 (8192 decimal) - MEM_RESERVE flag for VirtualAlloc
0x1000 (4096 decimal) - MEM_COMMIT flag for VirtualAlloc
0x8000 (32768 decimal) - MEM_RELEASE flag for VirtualFree
0x400 (1024 decimal) - Number of free list entries to initialize
0xf1 (241 decimal) - Free block size pattern mask
0xff (255 decimal) - Block header marker byte
0xf0 (240 decimal) - Block size field value
0x1000 (4096 decimal) - Block stride size

Error Handling:
- HeapAlloc failure: Returns NULL immediately
- VirtualAlloc reserve failure: Cleans up heap allocation if dynamic mode
- VirtualAlloc commit failure: Releases reserved memory and cleans up heap
- All cleanup paths properly restore system state before returning NULL

Structure Layout:
ErrorTableEntry repurposed as AllocatorDescriptor:
Offset  Size  Field Name          Type              Description
0x00    4     dwErrorCode         uint              Base pointer or link field  
0x04    4     lpszMessage         char *            Next pointer or link field
0x08    4     [field2].dwCode     uint              Free list start pointer
0x0C    4     [field2].lpMsg      char *            Memory descriptor pointer  
0x10    4     [field3].dwCode     uint              Virtual memory base
0x14    4     [field3].lpMsg      char *            Virtual memory end
0x18    ...   Free List Entries   ErrorTableEntry[] Array of 1024 free block entries

functions.name: FreeErrorTableEntry
functions.comment:
Free an error table entry and unlink it from the doubly-linked error table list.

Algorithm:
1. Free virtual memory region associated with error entry (VirtualFree at offset 0x10 with MEM_RELEASE flag 0x8000)
2. Check if entry is the current head of global error table list (PTR_g_aErrorTable_18__dwErrorCode_6ff38b90)
3. If head entry, update global head pointer to next entry (pNext at offset 0x4)
4. Check if entry is the sentinel node (g_aErrorTable + 0x12 = offset 0x6ff36b70)
5. If sentinel node, set DAT_6ff36b80 to 0xffffffff and return
6. If regular node, unlink from doubly-linked list by updating next/prev pointers
7. Free the error table entry structure memory using HeapFree with global heap handle

Parameters:
pErrorEntry: Pointer to ErrorTableEntry structure to deallocate

Returns:
void: No return value

Special Cases:
Sentinel node (at 0x6ff36b70): Sets global flag DAT_6ff36b80 to 0xffffffff instead of freeing
Head node: Updates global head pointer before unlinking from list

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x8000: MEM_RELEASE flag for VirtualFree (decimal 32768)
0x10: Offset to virtual memory handle in ErrorTableEntry structure (decimal 16)
0x4: Offset to pNext pointer in ErrorTableEntry structure (decimal 4)  
0x0: Offset to pPrev pointer in ErrorTableEntry structure (decimal 0)
0x6ff36b70: Address of sentinel error table node
0x6ff38b90: Global pointer to error table head entry
0x6ff36b80: Global flag modified when sentinel node is freed
0xffffffff: Value set in global flag when sentinel freed (decimal 4294967295)

Error Handling:
No explicit error checking performed on VirtualFree or HeapFree calls
Assumes valid ErrorTableEntry pointer passed as parameter
Relies on linked list structure integrity for safe unlinking operations

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | 4    | pNext      | void* | Pointer to next error table entry
0x04   | 4    | pPrev      | void* | Pointer to previous error table entry  
0x08   | 4    | dwReserved1| uint  | Reserved field (purpose unknown)
0x0C   | 4    | dwReserved2| uint  | Reserved field (purpose unknown)
0x10   | 4    | pVirtualMem| void* | Virtual memory handle for VirtualFree

functions.name: FreeMemoryPoolPages
functions.comment:
Frees virtual memory pages from managed memory pools

Algorithm:
1. Initialize pool traversal from global pool head pointer g_aErrorTable[0x12].lpszMessage
2. Skip pools with invalid virtual memory base (ppuVar4[4] == 0xffffffff)
3. Initialize page offset to 0x3ff000 (4MB - 4KB) and scan backwards through bitmap
4. For each bitmap entry marked as allocated (0xf0), attempt VirtualFree
5. Call VirtualFree with MEM_DECOMMIT (0x4000) to release 4KB page
6. Mark bitmap slot as freed (0xffffffff) and decrement global page counter
7. Update minimum free slot pointer if current slot is lower
8. Decrement target page count and exit early if quota reached
9. Continue scanning until beginning of pool (offset 0) reached
10. Check if all bitmap entries are free (0x400 consecutive 0xffffffff entries)
11. If pool is completely empty, call cleanup function FUN_6ff2f45e
12. Advance to next pool in linked list and repeat until quota met

Parameters:
nPageCount (int): Maximum number of 4KB pages to free from all pools

Returns:
void: No return value, modifies global pool state and memory allocation

Special Cases:
- Early exit when requested page count reached
- Skip pools with no virtual memory allocated
- Only update minimum free slot if current is lower than existing
- Pool cleanup only triggered when all 1024 bitmap entries are free
- Global page counter DAT_6ff3a058 decremented for each freed page

Magic Numbers:
0x3ff000 - Starting offset (4MB - 4KB) for backward bitmap scan
0x1000 - Page size (4KB) for VirtualFree operations  
0x4000 - MEM_DECOMMIT flag for VirtualFree
0xf0 - Bitmap entry indicating allocated page
0xffffffff - Bitmap entry indicating freed page
0x400 - Total bitmap entries per pool (1024 slots)
0x804 - Offset to bitmap data array (2052 bytes)

Structure Layout (MemoryPoolDescriptor):
Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type  | Description
-------|------|---------------|-------|----------------------------------
   0   |  4   | pHead         | void* | Head of pool list  
   4   |  4   | pNext         | void* | Next pool in linked list
   8   |  4   | dwReserved1   | uint  | Reserved field
  12   |  4   | pMinFreeSlot  | void* | Pointer to lowest free slot
  16   |  4   | pVirtualBase  | void* | Virtual memory base address
  20   |  4   | dwReserved2   | uint  | Reserved field  
  24   |  4   | dwPoolStatus  | uint  | Pool status flags
  28   |  4   | dwReserved3   | uint  | Reserved field
  32   | 8192 | aBitmapData   |uint[] | Page allocation bitmap (1024 entries)

Flag Bits:
0xf0 - Page allocated and committed
0xffffffff - Page freed and available

functions.name: ValidateAllocationBlockAddress
functions.signature: int ValidateAllocationBlockAddress(byte * pAddress, ErrorTableEntry * * ppTableEntry, uint * puBaseAddress)
functions.comment:
Validate memory address within allocation block and calculate adjusted address

Algorithm:
1. Initialize table pointer to g_aErrorTable[18] (offset 0x12 * 8 bytes)
2. Loop through linked error table entries checking address bounds
3. Compare address against entry's lower bound (offset 0x10) and upper bound (offset 0x14)
4. If address outside bounds, follow next pointer (offset 0x0) to continue search
5. Exit loop if reach sentinel value 0x6ff36b70 indicating end of table
6. Validate 16-byte alignment by checking (address & 0xf) == 0
7. Validate minimum offset by checking (address & 0xfff) >= 0x100
8. Store found table entry pointer in output parameter
9. Calculate 4KB-aligned base address using (address & 0xfffff000)
10. Store base address in output parameter  
11. Calculate final address: ((address - base - 0x100) >> 4) + 8 + base

Parameters:
pAddress (void*): Memory address to validate and process
ppTableEntry (ErrorTableEntry**): Output pointer for found error table entry
puBaseAddress (uint*): Output pointer for calculated 4KB base address

Returns:
0: Validation failed - address not found in table, misaligned, or offset too small
Non-zero: Calculated adjusted address based on base address and offset

Special Cases:
- Returns 0 if address not found in any table entry bounds
- Returns 0 if address not 16-byte aligned (address & 0xf != 0)  
- Returns 0 if offset within 4KB page less than 0x100 bytes
- Handles linked list traversal with sentinel check at 0x6ff36b70

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x12 (18): Starting offset in error table array
0xf (15): Alignment mask for 16-byte boundary check
0xfff (4095): Page offset mask for 4KB boundary
0x100 (256): Minimum required offset within page
0xfffff000: 4KB page base address mask
0x4 (4): Right shift amount for 16-byte block calculation
0x8 (8): Base offset added to final calculation
0x6ff36b70: Sentinel value marking end of error table list

Structure Layout:
ErrorTableEntry (8 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type                  | Description
0x00   | 4    | dwErrorCode   | ErrorTableEntry*      | Next entry pointer or error code
0x04   | 4    | lpszMessage   | char*                 | Error message string pointer

Address Bounds Check:
Offset 0x10: Lower bound address for allocation block
Offset 0x14: Upper bound address for allocation block

functions.name: UpdateMemoryPoolTracking
functions.signature: void UpdateMemoryPoolTracking(MemoryPool * pMemoryPool, uint dwAddress, byte * pbFlag)
functions.comment:
Updates memory pool tracking information and triggers cleanup when threshold reached.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate pointer to tracking entry in memory pool descriptor array
2. Add flag byte value to tracking entry allocation count  
3. Clear the input flag byte to zero
4. Set tracking entry status field to 0xf1 (active tracking)
5. Check if allocation count reached threshold (0xf0 = 240 allocations)
6. If threshold reached, increment global allocated pages counter
7. If global counter reaches 0x20 (32 pages), trigger memory cleanup

Parameters:
pMemoryPool - Pointer to MemoryPool structure containing tracking arrays
dwAddress - Virtual address used to calculate tracking entry index
pbFlag - Pointer to byte flag containing allocation count to add

Returns:
None (void function)

Special Cases:
Threshold of 0xf0 (240) allocations triggers page counting mechanism
Global threshold of 0x20 (32) pages triggers FreeMemoryPoolPages cleanup
Status value 0xf1 indicates active tracking state

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x10 - Base offset in memory pool structure for address calculations
0x18 - Array offset in memory pool structure for tracking entries  
0xc - Right shift count for address-to-index conversion (4096-byte pages)
0x8 - Size of each tracking entry (8 bytes: count + status)
0xf0 - Allocation count threshold (240 decimal)
0xf1 - Active tracking status marker
0x20 - Global page limit (32 decimal) before cleanup
0x10 - Parameter passed to FreeMemoryPoolPages for cleanup

Structure Layout:
MemoryPool tracking entry (8 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
+0x0   | 4    | nCount     | uint | Allocation count for this pool segment
+0x4   | 4    | dwStatus   | uint | Status flags (0xf1 = active tracking)

functions.name: AllocateMemoryFromPool
functions.comment:
Allocates memory from a managed pool using a linked list of memory allocators with fallback to VirtualAlloc.

Algorithm:

1. Traverse linked list of memory allocators starting from g_pErrorTableHead
2. For each active allocator (piVar8[4] != -1):
   - Search active memory blocks (offset 0x8 to 0x2018) for suitable free space
   - Check if requested size fits within block's available range  
   - Call FUN_6ff2f81a to attempt allocation from block
   - If successful, update block metadata and return pointer
   - If failed, update block end marker and continue search
3. Search lower priority blocks (offset 0x18 to end) using same allocation logic
4. If no space found in current allocator, advance to next allocator in list
5. If all existing allocators exhausted, find empty allocator slot in g_aErrorTable
6. For empty allocator: count consecutive free pages (up to 0x10 maximum)
7. Call VirtualAlloc to allocate physical memory for counted pages (page_count << 0xc bytes)
8. Call _memset to zero-initialize allocated memory 
9. Initialize each page with 0xF0 byte free space and link metadata
10. Set up allocator tracking structures and update global head pointer
11. Extract requested allocation from first initialized page
12. Return pointer to allocated memory + 0x100 offset, or NULL on failure

Parameters:

dwBytesToAllocate (uint) - Number of bytes to allocate from memory pool

Returns:

SUCCESS: Pointer to allocated memory block (base + 0x100 offset)
FAILURE: NULL (0x0) if allocation fails or VirtualAlloc fails

Special Cases:

- If allocator reaches end of list (circular check), searches for empty slots
- VirtualAlloc failure returns NULL immediately  
- Memory is zero-initialized after VirtualAlloc
- Each page provides 0xF0 (240) bytes of usable space
- Allocator metadata uses 0x10 bytes overhead per page
- Maximum consecutive pages per allocation: 0x10 (16 pages = 64KB)

Magic Numbers Reference:

0x100 (256) - Return pointer offset from memory block base
0xF0 (240) - Usable bytes per memory page after metadata overhead  
0xF1 (241) - Initial end marker for free space tracking
0x1000 (4096) - Virtual memory page size for VirtualAlloc
0x400 (1024) - Memory block stride in int* units (0x400 * 4 = 4096 bytes)
0x806 (2054) - End boundary for active block search range  
0x403 (1027) - Maximum entries in error table array
0x18 (24) - Allocator metadata overhead size
0x2018 (8216) - Upper boundary offset for active block range
0x10 (16) - Maximum consecutive pages for single allocation
0x3d (61) - Byte offset marker for page initialization flag (0xff)

Error Handling:

- VirtualAlloc failure: Returns NULL without cleanup
- FUN_6ff2f81a allocation failure: Updates block metadata and continues search  
- Empty allocator list: Calls InitializeMemoryAllocator() for bootstrap
- Invalid allocator state: Skips to next allocator in linked list
- Circular list detection: Breaks loop and searches for empty slots

Structure Layout:

ErrorTableEntry (8 bytes per entry):
Offset | Size | Field Name  | Type   | Description
-------|------|-------------|--------|------------------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | dwErrorCode | uint   | Error code or next pointer for linking
0x04   | 4    | lpszMessage | char * | Message pointer or memory tracking data

Memory Allocator Node Layout (accessed as int* array):
Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type  | Description  
-------|------|---------------|-------|------------------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | pNext         | int * | Next allocator in linked list
0x04   | 4    | pReserved     | int * | Reserved/unused field
0x08   | 4    | pMemoryStart  | int * | Pointer to first memory block entry
0x0C   | 4    | pMemoryEnd    | int * | Pointer to end of memory block array  
0x10   | 4    | pVirtualBase  | int * | Base address from VirtualAlloc
0x14   | 4    | dwReserved    | int   | Reserved/unused field

functions.name: AllocateBufferSpace
functions.signature: int AllocateBufferSpace(BufferManager * pBufferMgr, uint dwAvailableBytes, uint dwRequestedBytes)
functions.comment:
Allocates buffer space in managed buffer with chunk-based allocation

Algorithm:
1. Extract buffer boundary (pBufferMgr + 0xF8) and current position 
2. Check if remaining space (pBufferMgr->dwRemaining) is sufficient for request
3. If sufficient space available at current position, allocate directly
4. Otherwise, scan buffer starting from current position for available chunks
5. For each chunk, if first byte is 0, count consecutive zeros to find free space
6. If first byte is non-zero, advance by that value (skip allocated chunk)
7. When suitable free space found, mark first byte with marker value
8. Update buffer manager pointers: pCurrent advances by dwRequestedBytes
9. Calculate return value: (allocated_pointer * 16 - pBufferMgr * 15)

Parameters:
pBufferMgr: Pointer to BufferManager structure with allocation state
dwAvailableBytes: Total bytes available for allocation operations
dwRequestedBytes: Number of bytes to allocate from buffer

Returns:
int: Calculated handle/offset for allocated space, 0 on failure

Special Cases:
- Returns 0 if insufficient space available
- Returns 0 if buffer boundary would be exceeded
- Handles buffer wraparound by resetting to base pointer (offset 8)
- Marker value placed at allocation start for tracking

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name  | Type     | Description
-------|------|-------------|----------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | pCurrent    | void*    | Current allocation position
0x04   | 4    | dwRemaining | uint     | Bytes remaining at current pos
0x08   | 4    | pBase       | void*    | Base buffer pointer for reset
...    | 236  | padding     | byte[236]| Reserved space
0xF8   | 4    | pEnd        | void*    | End boundary pointer

functions.name: AdjustFileBufferBounds
functions.signature: int AdjustFileBufferBounds(int * pMemPool, int * pSize, byte * pBuffer, uint dwNewSize)
functions.comment:
Adjusts the size of a memory buffer within a constrained allocation pool.

Algorithm:
  1. Load current buffer size from pBuffer[0]
  2. Calculate pool entry address: pMemPool[0x18 + ((pBuffer - pMemPool[0x10]) >> 0xc) * 8]
  3. Compare newSize against currentSize:
     - If newSize < currentSize: shrink operation, return freed bytes to pool with marker 0xf1
     - If newSize == currentSize: no change required, return success
     - If newSize > currentSize: expand operation, validate zero-padding from currentSize to newSize
  4. For expansion, validate buffer space constraints:
     - Check newSize does not exceed pool boundary (pMemPool + 0xf8)
     - Scan all bytes from currentSize to newSize, all must be zero
  5. Update buffer size field to newSize
  6. If payload pointer at pSize[0] falls within buffer range, adjust pointer to newSize
  7. Count zero bytes following payload (stored in pSize[1]) for size tracking
  8. Update pool free space accounting at pMemPool[0x18]
  9. Return success (1) or failure (0) on validation errors

Parameters:
  pMemPool: Pointer to memory pool structure, contains offsets 0x10 (base), 0x18 (free space)
  pSize: Pointer to size tracking structure (2 DWORDs): [0] = payload pointer, [1] = size
  pBuffer: Byte pointer to buffer being resized, pBuffer[0] contains current size
  dwNewSize: New size in bytes (0x0 to 0xf8 bytes relative to buffer start)

Returns:
  1 (success) if resize operation completed with all validations passing
  0 (failure) if any validation failed: boundary exceeded, padding not all-zeros, pointer adjustment failed
  On failure: buffer size and pool state remain unchanged

Special Cases:
  - Expansion requires entire padding region to be zero-filled (detects overlapping allocations)
  - Payload pointer within buffer triggers pointer and size recalculation
  - Pool boundary check prevents buffer overflow (max size = 0xf8 bytes)
  - Shrink returns freed bytes to pool accounting immediately
  - Marker 0xf1 written to indicate pool entry was modified

functions.name: UpdateFpuControlBits
functions.signature: uint UpdateFpuControlBits(void * this, uint param_1, uint param_2)
functions.comment:
Modifies specific bits in the floating point unit control word register.

Algorithm:
1. Save current FPU control word to stack using FSTCW instruction
2. Combine saved control word with upper 16 bits of context pointer into composite value
3. Retrieve current FPU control word value via GetFpuControlWord()
4. Apply bit mask operation: (current & ~dwBitMask) | (dwNewBits & dwBitMask)
5. Set updated FPU control word via SetFpuControlWord()
6. Restore original FPU control word from stack using FLDCW instruction
7. Return the updated control word value

Parameters:
- this (void*): Context pointer (upper 16 bits used in composite value)
- dwNewBits (uint): New bit values to apply where mask is set
- dwBitMask (uint): Bit mask indicating which bits to modify (1=modify, 0=preserve)

Returns:
- uint: Updated FPU control word value after applying bit modifications

Special Cases:
- If dwBitMask is 0x0000, function returns current control word unchanged
- If dwBitMask is 0xFFFF, function returns dwNewBits (full replacement)
- IMPLICIT: Original FPU control word is preserved and restored

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x10: Bit shift for extracting upper 16 bits of context pointer
- FSTCW: Store FPU Control Word (saves current state)
- FLDCW: Load FPU Control Word (restores saved state)

Error Handling:
- Function assumes valid context pointer and control word operations
- No validation of bit mask or new bit values
- FPU control word operations are atomic at instruction level

functions.comment: Setting prototype: void ApplyFpuControlBitMask(InitContext* pInitContext, uint dwNewBits, uint dwFullFlags)

functions.name: GetFpuControlWord
functions.comment:
Convert FPU control flags from one format to another for FPU control register updates.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize target flags to 0
2. Test source flag bit 0 (0x01) - if set, OR target with 0x10 (exception enable bit 4)
3. Test source flag bit 2 (0x04) - if set, OR target with 0x08 (exception enable bit 3) 
4. Test source flag bit 3 (0x08) - if set, OR target with 0x04 (exception enable bit 2)
5. Test source flag bit 4 (0x10) - if set, OR target with 0x02 (exception enable bit 1)
6. Test source flag bit 5 (0x20) - if set, OR target with 0x01 (exception enable bit 0)
7. Test source flag bit 1 (0x02) - if set, OR target with 0x80000 (special control bit)
8. Extract precision control bits (bits 10-11, mask 0xc00) from source
9. Map precision control: 0x400->0x100, 0x800->0x200, 0xc00->0x300
10. Extract rounding control bits (bits 8-9, mask 0x300) from source
11. Map rounding control: 0x00->0x20000, 0x200->0x10000, others->no change
12. Test source flag bit 12 (0x1000) - if set, OR target with 0x40000
13. Return converted target flags

Parameters:
dwSourceFlags - Input FPU control flags in source format to be converted

Returns:
Converted FPU control flags in target format for hardware register update

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x01 - Source exception enable bit 0 -> Target bit 4 (0x10)
0x02 - Source special control bit -> Target bit 19 (0x80000)
0x04 - Source exception enable bit 2 -> Target bit 3 (0x08)
0x08 - Source exception enable bit 3 -> Target bit 2 (0x04)
0x10 - Source exception enable bit 4 -> Target bit 1 (0x02)
0x20 - Source exception enable bit 5 -> Target bit 0 (0x01)
0x300 - Rounding control mask (bits 8-9)
0xc00 - Precision control mask (bits 10-11)
0x1000 - Source control bit 12 -> Target bit 18 (0x40000)
0x10000 - Target rounding mode: round towards nearest
0x20000 - Target rounding mode: round towards zero (truncate)
0x100, 0x200, 0x300 - Target precision control values
0x40000 - Target control bit for infinity control

Flag Bits:
Source Format Bits -> Target Format Bits
Bit 0 (0x01): Exception mask 0 -> Exception enable 4 (0x10)
Bit 1 (0x02): Special control -> Control bit 19 (0x80000)  
Bit 2 (0x04): Exception mask 2 -> Exception enable 3 (0x08)
Bit 3 (0x08): Exception mask 3 -> Exception enable 2 (0x04)
Bit 4 (0x10): Exception mask 4 -> Exception enable 1 (0x02)
Bit 5 (0x20): Exception mask 5 -> Exception enable 0 (0x01)
Bits 8-9 (0x300): Rounding control -> Rounding mode (0x10000/0x20000)
Bits 10-11 (0xc00): Precision control -> Precision mode (0x100/0x200/0x300)
Bit 12 (0x1000): Infinity control -> Control bit 18 (0x40000)

functions.name: ConvertFpuControlToMxcsr
functions.comment:
Converts x87 FPU control word bit flags to SSE MXCSR control register format.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize result to 0 and extract invalid operation mask from bit 4 of FPU control word
2. Convert FPU exception mask bits to MXCSR format:
   - Bit 3 (divide-by-zero) → MXCSR bit 2 (0x04)
   - Bit 2 (denormal) → MXCSR bit 3 (0x08) 
   - Bit 1 (overflow) → MXCSR bit 4 (0x10)
   - Bit 0 (underflow) → MXCSR bit 5 (0x20)
3. Convert FPU flush-to-zero from bit 19 (0x80000) to MXCSR bit 1 (0x02)
4. Extract and convert rounding mode from bits 8-9 (0x300):
   - 0x100 (round to nearest) → MXCSR bits 10-11 (0x400)
   - 0x200 (round down) → MXCSR bit 11 (0x800)
   - 0x300 (round up) → MXCSR bits 10-11 (0xC00)
5. Convert precision control from bits 16-17 (0x30000):
   - 0x00000 (24-bit) → MXCSR bits 8-9 (0x300)
   - 0x10000 (53-bit) → MXCSR bit 9 (0x200)
   - 0x20000 (64-bit) → No MXCSR equivalent (default)
6. Convert infinity control from bit 18 (0x40000) to MXCSR bit 12 (0x1000)

Parameters:
  dwFpuControlWord - x87 FPU control word containing exception masks, rounding mode, precision control

Returns:
  Equivalent MXCSR control register value with converted bit flags

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x10 (16) - FPU invalid operation mask bit
  0x08 (8) - FPU divide-by-zero mask bit  
  0x04 (4) - FPU denormal operand mask bit
  0x02 (2) - FPU overflow mask bit
  0x01 (1) - FPU underflow mask bit
  0x80000 (524288) - FPU flush-to-zero flag
  0x300 (768) - FPU rounding mode mask (bits 8-9)
  0x100 (256) - Round to nearest even
  0x200 (512) - Round toward negative infinity
  0x300 (768) - Round toward positive infinity
  0x30000 (196608) - FPU precision control mask (bits 16-17)
  0x10000 (65536) - 53-bit precision (double)
  0x40000 (262144) - FPU infinity control bit
  0x400 (1024) - MXCSR round to nearest (bits 13-14)
  0x800 (2048) - MXCSR round down (bit 14)
  0xC00 (3072) - MXCSR round up (bits 13-14)
  0x1000 (4096) - MXCSR denormals-are-zero flag

functions.name: CheckBitfieldSlotAvailable
functions.comment:
Checks if a bit position in a 32-bit DWORD array is available (clear) and all subsequent DWORDs are also clear.

Algorithm:

1. Calculate target DWORD index by dividing bit index by 32 (0x20)
2. Calculate bit position within DWORD using modulo operation
3. Create bit mask using left shift and bitwise NOT to test target bit
4. Test if target bit is set - if so, position is unavailable, return false
5. Calculate starting array index (DWORD index + 1) for subsequent checks
6. If starting index is less than 3, iterate through remaining array elements
7. Check each DWORD from starting index to index 2 (3 total DWORDs maximum)
8. If any DWORD contains non-zero value, position is unavailable, return false
9. If all checks pass, position is available, return true

Parameters:
- pdwBitfield: Pointer to DWORD array used as bitfield (minimum 3 DWORDs, 12 bytes)
- nBitIndex: Zero-based bit position to check (0-95 for 3 DWORD array)

Returns:
- true (1): Bit position is clear and all subsequent DWORDs are zero
- false (0): Bit position is set OR subsequent DWORDs contain non-zero values

Special Cases:
- If bit index results in DWORD index 2 or higher, no subsequent DWORD checking needed
- Function assumes array has at least 3 DWORDs (indices 0, 1, 2)
- Uses 32-bit arithmetic for bit calculations (0x20 = 32, 0x1f = 31)

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x20 (32): Bits per DWORD for index calculation
- 0x1f (31): Maximum bit position within DWORD (bit mask)
- 0x1fU (31): Unsigned constant for bit position calculation
- 3: Maximum array index checked (indices 0, 1, 2)
- 4: Byte increment for DWORD pointer arithmetic

functions.name: ClearBitArrayRange
functions.comment:
Process bitmap bits from specified offset through end of buffer

Algorithm:
1. Calculate word index (nBitOffset / 32) and bit offset within word (nBitOffset % 32)
2. Create bit mask for starting position: 1 << (31 - bit_offset)
3. Call ProcessBitOperation on first word with calculated mask
4. If operation returns 0, exit (typically indicates completion)
5. Decrement word index
6. Loop through remaining words from current to word 0 with mask=1
7. Each iteration: call ProcessBitOperation, check result, decrement index
8. Exit when all words processed or operation returns 0

Parameters:
  pBitmapBase (dword *) - Base pointer to 32-bit word array containing bitmap
  nBitOffset (int) - Starting bit offset into bitmap

Returns:
  void - Operation result indicated by side effects in buffer

Special Cases:
  - If nBitOffset >= total bits in buffer, behavior depends on loop guard
  - First word uses masked operation, subsequent words use mask=1
  - Early exit when operation returns non-zero value
  - Note: EDI register used as pBitmapWord pointer throughout function

Magic Numbers:
  0x20 (32) - Bits per word for division to get word index
  0x1f (31) - Bit position for creating shift mask
  1 - Mask value for complete word in loop

Structure Layout:
Bitmap is an array of 32-bit words where each bit position represents a flag or state:
  Offset | Size | Meaning
  -------|------|--------
  +0     |  4   | Word N (32 bits)

functions.name: ClearBitAndTruncateHigh
functions.comment:
Clears a bit at the specified index and truncates all higher bits in a 96-bit bitfield.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate word index by dividing bit index by 0x20 (32)
2. Calculate bit position within word using modulo 0x20
3. Get pointer to the target 32-bit word in the bitfield
4. Calculate bit shift value as (0x1F - bit_position)
5. Check if the target bit is currently set using bit mask
6. If bit is set and no higher bits are set (via CheckBitfieldSlotAvailable), call FUN_1001fde6 with previous index
7. Clear the target bit using AND with inverted bit mask
8. Calculate starting word for high-bit clearing (word_index + 1)
9. If more words exist (word_index < 2), clear all remaining high words
10. Return the value from step 6 or 0 if bit was not set

Parameters:
pBitfield - Pointer to 96-bit bitfield (3 x 32-bit words, 12 bytes total)
nBitIndex - Zero-based bit position to clear (0-95 range)

Returns:
Integer value from FUN_1001fde6 if bit was set and no higher bits exist, 0 otherwise

Special Cases:
Bitfield is exactly 96 bits (3 x 32-bit words)
Bit index 0x20 (32) targets second word, 0x40 (64) targets third word
Higher bit clearing always clears from next word boundary to end

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x20 (32) - Bits per word, used for word boundary calculations
0x1F (31) - Bit mask for position within word
0x3 (3) - Total number of 32-bit words in 96-bit bitfield

Error Handling:
No bounds checking on bit index - caller must ensure 0 <= nBitIndex <= 95
No null pointer validation on pBitfield parameter

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type | Description
0x00   | 4    | dwLowBits     | uint | Bits 0-31
0x04   | 4    | dwMidBits     | uint | Bits 32-63  
0x08   | 4    | dwHighBits    | uint | Bits 64-95

functions.name: CopyThreeIntegers
functions.comment:
Copies three consecutive 32-bit integers from source to destination using offset-based addressing.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate offset between destination address and source pointer address
2. Initialize counter to 3 for three integer copy operations
3. Enter copy loop:
   a. Read current source integer value
   b. Store value at destination using calculated offset + current source position
   c. Advance source pointer by 4 bytes (one integer)
   d. Decrement counter
   e. Continue while counter > 0
4. Return when all three integers copied

Parameters:
- nDestination (int): Target memory address where integers will be copied
- pSource (uint *): Source pointer to array of 32-bit unsigned integers

Returns:
- void: No return value, performs in-place memory copy operation

Special Cases:
- Function always copies exactly 3 integers (12 bytes total)
- Uses pointer arithmetic with offset calculation for addressing
- No bounds checking or validation performed

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x3 (3): Fixed number of integers to copy
- 0x4 (4): Size increment per iteration (sizeof(uint))
- 0x1 (1): Decrement value for loop counter

functions.name: ZeroFloatComponents
functions.comment:
Zeros three consecutive 32-bit floating-point component values.

Algorithm:
1. Load target address into EDI from stack parameter
2. Clear EAX register to zero
3. Store zero to first component [EDI] and increment EDI by 4
4. Store zero to second component [EDI+4] and increment EDI by 4  
5. Store zero to third component [EDI+8] and increment EDI by 4
6. Restore EDI register and return

Parameters:
pFloatComponents (uint *): Pointer to array of 3 consecutive 32-bit values representing floating-point components (mantissa, exponent, sign or similar decomposition)

Returns:
void: No return value

Special Cases:
Uses optimized STOSD instruction for efficient zeroing of 32-bit values
Assembly utilizes string instruction auto-increment for consecutive memory writes

functions.name: CheckArrayFirstThreeZero
functions.comment:
Checks whether the first three integers in an array are all zero.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize loop counter (nIndex) to 0
2. Enter do-while loop for three iterations
3. Check if current array element is non-zero
4. If non-zero found, return 0 (false) immediately
5. Increment loop counter and advance array pointer by 4 bytes
6. Continue loop while counter < 3
7. If all three elements are zero, return 1 (true)

Parameters:
  pnArray - int * - Pointer to integer array to check (must have at least 3 elements)

Returns:
  1 - All first three elements are zero (validation passed)
  0 - At least one of the first three elements is non-zero (validation failed)

Special Cases:
  Function assumes pnArray points to valid memory with at least 3 integers
  No null pointer validation performed - caller must ensure valid array

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x3 (3) - Number of array elements to check
  0x4 (4) - Size of int in bytes for pointer arithmetic

functions.name: ShiftBigIntegerRight
functions.comment:
Performs right bit shift operation on 128-bit integer stored as 4-element uint32 array.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate word shifts (dwShiftCount / 0x20) and bit shifts (dwShiftCount % 0x20)
2. Initialize carry accumulator (param_2 = 0) and bit shift amount (byBitShifts)
3. For each of 4 array elements (index 0-3):
   a. Load current element value (dwCurrentElement)
   b. Shift element right by bit amount, OR with previous carry
   c. Calculate new carry from bits being shifted out
   d. Store shifted result back to array element
   e. Advance to next element pointer
4. Handle additional word-level shifts for elements 2 down to 0:
   a. If source index < word shifts: clear destination element (set to 0)
   b. Otherwise: copy element from shifted source position
   c. Decrement both source index and destination offset by 4 bytes

Parameters:
  pBigInteger: Pointer to 4-element uint32 array representing 128-bit integer
  dwShiftCount: Number of bits to shift right (0-127 valid range)

Returns:
  void - Operation modifies array in-place

Special Cases:
  - Shift count 0: No operation performed, array unchanged
  - Shift count >= 32: Combines bit shifts with word-level element movement
  - Shift count >= 128: All elements become 0 (complete right shift out)

Magic Numbers:
  0x20 (32): Bits per 32-bit word, used for word/bit shift separation
  0x1f (31): Bit mask for shift amount (ensures valid 0-31 bit shifts)
  0x3: Initial element counter (processes 4 elements: indices 0,1,2,3)
  0x8 (8): Starting byte offset for element 2 (8 = 2 * sizeof(uint32))
  0x2: Starting element index for reverse copy (element 2)

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field       | Type | Description
-------|------|-------------|------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | element[0]  | uint | Least significant 32 bits
0x04   | 4    | element[1]  | uint | Second 32-bit word  
0x08   | 4    | element[2]  | uint | Third 32-bit word
0x0C   | 4    | element[3]  | uint | Most significant 32 bits

Error Handling:
  - No bounds checking on shift count parameter
  - Caller responsible for ensuring valid array pointer
  - Large shift counts (>= 128) result in all-zero array

functions.name: AdjustValueWithBitOps
functions.signature: int AdjustValueWithBitOps(ExtendedFloat * pInputFloat, uint * pOutputData, ConversionConfig * pConfig)
functions.comment:
Converts extended precision floating-point number to target precision format

Algorithm:
1. Extract exponent and sign from input extended float structure
2. Load mantissa components (low, mid, high) into local variables  
3. Check for zero exponent (special case: -0x3FFF indicates zero/denormalized)
4. If zero exponent, test mantissa for actual zero using CheckArrayFirstThreeZero
5. If true zero, set result code to 0 and clear mantissa components
6. For normal numbers, backup mantissa using CopyThreeIntegers
7. Clear high bits and truncate using ClearBitAndTruncateHigh based on precision
8. Adjust exponent if truncation occurred (increment by 1)
9. Check exponent bounds against config limits (min/max exponent range)
10. Handle underflow: clear mantissa if exponent below minimum range
11. Handle overflow: set infinity bit (0x80000000) if exponent exceeds maximum
12. For in-range values, restore mantissa and apply precision shifts
13. Combine adjusted exponent, sign bit, and mantissa into output word
14. Store result in 32-bit or 64-bit format based on output configuration

Parameters:
pInputFloat - Pointer to ExtendedFloat structure containing 12-byte extended precision value
pOutputData - Pointer to output buffer for converted floating-point data  
pConfig - Pointer to ConversionConfig structure with precision and range parameters

Returns:
0 - Input was zero or resulted in zero after conversion
1 - Overflow occurred, result is infinity 
2 - Normal conversion completed successfully

Structure Layout:
ExtendedFloat (12 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name           Type    Description
0x00    2     wMantissaLow        ushort  Low 16 bits of mantissa
0x02    4     dwMantissaMid       uint    Middle 32 bits of mantissa  
0x06    4     dwMantissaHigh      uint    High 32 bits of mantissa
0x0A    2     wExponentAndSign    ushort  Exponent (bits 0-14) and sign (bit 15)

ConversionConfig (24 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name           Type    Description
0x00    4     dwMaxExponent       uint    Maximum allowed exponent value
0x04    4     dwNormalizedExponent uint   Exponent for normalized range  
0x08    4     dwPrecisionBits     uint    Number of precision bits to maintain
0x0C    4     dwMantissaBits      uint    Mantissa bit width for shifts
0x10    4     dwOutputBits        uint    Output format (0x20=32-bit, 0x40=64-bit)
0x14    4     dwExponentBias      uint    Bias value added to final exponent

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x3FFF: Extended precision exponent bias
- Magic number 0x7FFF: Exponent mask (excludes sign bit)  
- Magic number 0x8000: Sign bit mask in exponent field
- Magic number 0x80000000: Infinity/overflow indicator in mantissa
- Magic number 0x1F: Shift mask for mantissa bit positioning

functions.name: FormatFloatingPointDigits
functions.signature: void FormatFloatingPointDigits(char * szOutputBuffer, int nDigitCount, FloatFormatState * pFormatState)
functions.comment:
Formats floating-point digit string with optional rounding and exponent adjustment

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output buffer with leading zero ('0') 
2. Copy source digits from format state to output buffer, padding with zeros
3. Null-terminate the digit string
4. Apply rounding if next source digit >= '5' by incrementing from right
5. Handle carry propagation through consecutive '9' digits  
6. Adjust exponent if first digit becomes '1' after rounding
7. Shift digits left if no leading '1' to normalize output

Parameters:
  szOutputBuffer - Output buffer to receive formatted digit string
  nDigitCount - Number of significant digits to format
  pFormatState - Pointer to FloatFormatState structure

Returns:
  void - Results stored in szOutputBuffer and pFormatState->nExponent updated

Special Cases:
  - If nDigitCount <= 0, outputs single '0' and null terminator
  - Source digit exhaustion fills remainder with '0' characters  
  - Rounding '999...9' propagates carry to create leading '1' 
  - Leading '1' after rounding increments exponent and shifts digits

Structure Layout:
  FloatFormatState (16 bytes):
    Offset  Size  Field Name     Type     Description
    0x00    4     dwReserved     uint     Reserved field 
    0x04    4     nExponent      int      Current exponent value
    0x08    4     dwReserved2    uint     Reserved field

- FUN_6f9e8470: Finalize digit array

functions.name: ConvertDoubleToExtended
functions.comment:
Convert IEEE 754 double precision (64-bit) to extended precision (80-bit) floating-point format.

Algorithm:
1. Extract exponent (11 bits) and sign bit from double precision format at offset +6
2. Extract mantissa components from double precision low and high words
3. Handle special cases: zero values (both parts zero) set output to zero and return
4. Handle infinity/NaN: if exponent is 0x7FF (2047), set extended exponent to 0x7FFF (32767)
5. Handle denormalized numbers: if exponent is 0, set bias to 0x3C01 (15361) and clear hidden bit
6. Normal numbers: convert exponent bias from double (1023) to extended (16383) by adding 0x3C00
7. Construct extended precision mantissa by combining double parts with proper bit alignment
8. Normalize mantissa by left-shifting until MSB is set, adjusting exponent accordingly
9. Store final extended precision format: mantissa in pExtended[0-1], exponent+sign in pExtended[2]

Parameters:
pExtended - Pointer to output extended precision float (12 bytes: mantissa[8], exponent[2], padding[2])
pDouble - Pointer to input double precision float (8 bytes: low[4], high[4])

Returns:
void - Result stored in pExtended output buffer

Special Cases:
Zero Input: Both pDouble[0] and pDouble[1] mantissa bits zero - outputs zero extended precision
Infinity: Double exponent 0x7FF becomes extended exponent 0x7FFF  
NaN: Double exponent 0x7FF with non-zero mantissa preserved as extended NaN
Denormalized: Double exponent 0x000 handled with special bias and normalization

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x7FF0 - Double precision exponent mask (11 bits shifted left 4)
0x7FF - Maximum double precision exponent (infinity/NaN marker)
0x7FFF - Maximum extended precision exponent (infinity/NaN marker)  
0x3C00 - Exponent bias conversion offset (16383 - 1023 = 15360)
0x3C01 - Denormalized number bias for extended precision (15361)
0x80000000 - Extended precision hidden bit mask
0x8000 - Sign bit mask for extended precision format
0xFFFFF - Double precision mantissa mask (20 bits)
0x15 - Bit shift count (21) for mantissa alignment
0xB - Bit shift count (11) for mantissa reconstruction

IEEE 754 Format Layout:
Double Precision (64-bit): [Sign:1][Exponent:11][Mantissa:52]
Extended Precision (80-bit): [Sign:1][Exponent:15][Hidden:1][Mantissa:63]

Error Handling:
No explicit error checking - assumes valid double precision input
Invalid inputs may produce undefined extended precision results

functions.name: CopyStringOptimized
functions.comment:
Optimized string copy function that efficiently copies null-terminated strings
using word-aligned memory operations and bitwise null detection for maximum
performance on x86 architecture.

Algorithm:
1. Check source pointer alignment against 4-byte boundary (szSource & 3)
2. Copy bytes individually until source reaches word alignment
3. Check each copied byte for null terminator, exit early if found
4. Begin optimized word-level copying once aligned
5. Load 32-bit words from source and apply null detection algorithm
6. Use magic constant 0x7efefeff to detect null bytes within words
7. When null detected, determine exact byte position using bit masks
8. Copy final bytes and null terminator based on detected position
9. Return original destination pointer

Parameters:
szDestination (char*): Destination buffer where string will be copied
szSource (char*): Source null-terminated string to copy

Returns:
char*: Returns szDestination (original destination buffer address)

Special Cases:
Empty string (first byte is null) handled correctly by early exit
Source and destination buffers must not overlap (undefined behavior)
Destination buffer must be large enough to hold entire source string

Magic Numbers:
0x7efefeff: Magic constant for fast null byte detection in 32-bit words
0x81010100: Bit mask for isolating overflow bits from null detection
0xffffffff: XOR mask component of null detection algorithm  
0x3: Bit mask for checking 4-byte memory alignment

functions.name: OptimizedStringCopy
functions.comment:
Performs optimized string copying using word-aligned memory access and null-byte detection.
This function implements a high-performance strcpy equivalent using x86 alignment optimization.
Uses magic constants to detect null terminators within 32-bit words for maximum throughput.
Handles both aligned and unaligned source/destination buffers gracefully.

Algorithm:
1. Check destination pointer alignment against 4-byte word boundary
2. Copy unaligned bytes one-by-one until destination reaches word alignment  
3. Enter optimized loop processing 4-byte words from aligned destination
4. Apply magic constant 0x7EFEFEFF to detect null bytes within words
5. Use mask 0x81010100 to isolate carry bits indicating null presence
6. When null detected in word, determine exact byte position and handle
7. Switch to source processing with similar alignment optimization
8. Copy source bytes individually until source is word-aligned
9. Process aligned source words until null terminator found
10. Terminate destination string with null and return original pointer

Parameters:
lpszDestination - Pointer to destination buffer with sufficient space allocated
lpcszSource - Pointer to source null-terminated string to be copied

Returns:
Returns lpszDestination pointer for function chaining operations

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x7EFEFEFF (2130640639) - Magic additive constant for null detection algorithm
0x81010100 (2164391168) - Bit mask to isolate null detection carry flags  
0x3 (3) - Alignment mask for checking 4-byte word boundaries
0xFF0000 (16711680) - Third byte mask for null position detection
0xFF000000 (4278190080) - Fourth byte mask for null position detection

Special Cases:
Empty source string copies only null terminator to destination
Overlapping memory regions produce undefined behavior per C standard
Destination buffer must accommodate source length plus null terminator
Algorithm assumes little-endian x86 architecture for bit manipulation

functions.name: CloseAndDeallocateExtraStreams
functions.comment:
Closes and deallocates extra file stream structures beyond the reserved slots.

Algorithm:
1. Acquire critical section 2 (stream table lock)
2. Iterate through stream structures starting from index 3 (skip reserved 0-2)
3. For each non-null stream with active flags (0x83 = read/write/error):
   a. Call ThreadSafeFileClose to close the file
   b. If close succeeds (not -1), increment closed count
4. For indices >= 20 (0x14), cleanup dynamically allocated streams:
   a. Delete the embedded critical section at offset 0x20
   b. Deallocate the stream structure memory
   c. Clear the table entry to NULL
5. Release critical section 2
6. Return count of successfully closed files

Parameters:
  None (void)

Returns:
  int - Number of files successfully closed

Flag Bits (0x83 mask):
  0x01 - _IOREAD  (file open for reading)
  0x02 - _IOWRT   (file open for writing)
  0x80 - _IOERR   (error occurred)

Stream Table Layout:
  Indices 0-2:   Reserved/system streams (stdin, stdout, stderr)
  Indices 3-19:  Standard stream slots (close only, no dealloc)
  Indices 20+:   Dynamically allocated streams (close + dealloc)

Structure Layout (stream at g_pStreamStructureTable[n]):
  Offset  Size  Field           Description
  0x00    0x20  FILE            Standard C FILE structure
  0x20    0x18  CRITICAL_SECTION Embedded lock for thread safety

functions.name: ValidateStreamPropertyId
functions.comment:
Maps Windows API error codes to standardized stream error values.

Algorithm:

  2. Iterate through error mapping table starting at 0x6fd4b650 (step by 8 bytes)
  3. If dwErrorCode matches table entry, store mapped value and return
  4. Check range 0x13-0x24: map to 0xd
  5. Check range 0xbc-0xca: map to 0x8
  6. Default mapping: use 0x16

Parameters:
  dwErrorCode - Windows error code from GetLastError() or API call

Returns:
  None (void). Sets global error value via FUN_6fd2761d

Special Cases:
  Error Range Mapping Table:
  Range 0x13-0x24 (19-36)  -> Standard error 0xd (13)
  Range 0xbc-0xca (188-202) -> Standard error 0x8 (8)
  All other values          -> Default 0x16 (22)
  Table values at 0x6fd4b650-0x6fd4b7b8 contain (code, mapped_value) pairs
